channel.title: Finomik blog
channel.description: Classroom ideas, data on financial education and news from Finomik.

item.title: Our new website: the new face of Finomik
item.description: We've rebuilt our website so any school can try the platform before talking to us: the simulator, the challenges, Finny and the teacher dashboard, all with sample data.

item.title: Almost half of adults couldn't face an unexpected expense without serious difficulty
item.description: According to the World Bank's Global Findex 2021, only 55% of adults in developing economies could get extra money for an emergency within 30 days without much difficulty. For everyone else, a surprise expense becomes a problem.

item.title: Almost 1 in 5 15-year-olds don't reach the baseline level of financial literacy
item.description: In the PISA 2022 financial literacy assessment, 18% of 15-year-olds across the OECD fell below the baseline level: they couldn't reliably apply financial knowledge to everyday situations, such as reading a bill or comparing two offers. We're not talking about investing or long-term planning, but the minimum needed to get by in everyday economic life.

item.title: 3.5 billion adults worldwide lack basic financial knowledge
item.description: According to the global survey by S&P, Gallup and the World Bank, around 3.5 billion adults lack the minimum financial knowledge to make informed decisions. It isn't an abstract figure: it's the share of humanity managing its income, its debts and its future without the tools to do it well.

item.title: Answer instead of reread: up to 50% more recall one week later
item.description: It isn't just that students prefer challenges to textbooks. Answering questions forces you to retrieve what you've learned, and that fixes knowledge far better than rereading. In Roediger and Karpicke's classic experiment (2006), those who practised by answering remembered around 50% more one week later.

item.title: Only 33% of adults worldwide have basic financial literacy
item.description: In 2015, S&P Ratings, Gallup and the World Bank carried out the largest financial literacy study ever: 150,000 adults interviewed in 148 countries. The conclusion was blunt: only 1 in 3 adults worldwide understands basic financial concepts such as compound interest, inflation or risk diversification.

item.title: 88% of adults want compulsory financial education in high school
item.description: When you ask adults, the answer is clear. In a National Endowment for Financial Education survey (NEFE, 2022), 88% of US adults said their state should require a financial education course to graduate from high school. It isn't a fringe demand: it's a generational one.
